reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 5.1 contains only a care-and-skill services warranty, and there is no conformance warranty period or repair/replace/refund remedy anywhere, while Section 5.4(c) places all Materials on an 'AS IS' basis — this fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies) on two material terms, so it is not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

Redline is actionable and correctly targeted: a new Section 5.1(c) adds a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Deliverables/Materials plus the at-Vendor's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and the 'EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1' lead-in carves the express warranty out of the AS IS disclaimer, matching the redline guidance.

Placing the new warranty inside Section 5.1 neutralises the exclusivity language in Section 5.2 (p0065) without needing a separate edit there, so the edit is close to minimal; the 0.474 changed-character ratio on p0074 reflects only the required carve-out prefix in an all-caps sentence.

Failed 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' check is a regex phrasing artifact — the inserted text expressly states 'a period of ninety (90) days following delivery', which satisfies the fallback/preferred services period.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position and explains both edits; the residual gap (5.4(a)-(b) error-free/defect-correction disclaimers not separately carved out) is a minor sub-element that does not undermine the finding.
